SECOND AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH KPMG LLP FOR CONSULTATION AND/OR FORENSIC ACCOUNTANT SERVICES WHEREAS, pursuant to Contract No. L-640 (the “Contract”), filed with the office of the Metropolitan Clerk on November 21, 2002, the Department of Law of The Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County engaged KMPG LLP to provide consulting and forensic accounting services in connection with a fire at the Nashville Thermal Transfer Plant on May 23, 2002; and WHEREAS, the Contract provides that the maximum compensation that may be earned by KMPG thereunder is one hundred and five thousand dollars ($105,000) as amended; and WHEREAS, the parties agree that scope of work contemplated under the original contract be expanded to include assistance in the accumulation of source documents, and the drafting of advances and claim materials, as indicated in the document attached as Exhibit A Therefore, the allowable compensation limit should be raised to two hundred twenty five thousand dollars ($225,000) to permit KMPG to complete all required tasks. Now, therefore, the parties agree that the Contract shall be modified as follows: The sixth sentence of Paragraph 3 shall be changed to read: The total compensation paid to Contractor (including expenses) under this Contract shall not exceed two hundred twenty five thousand dollars ($225,000). All of the provisions of the Contract shall remain in full force and effect except as specifically modified by this amendment. Exhibit A Statement of Work KPMG’s scope of work under this agreement shall include: 1, Coverage review and application to the loss. Tasks include: Investigation, assembly and documentation of the facts; research coverage interpretations and identification of areas of insured and uninsured loss. This would address all property damage and time element loss of the Insured.
2. Loss analysis. Tasks include: Investigation and accumulation of source documents, records analysis, trend evaluation, and compilation of "actual loss sustained" for property and operations.
3. Assistance in the preparation and presentation of the claim. Tasks include: Report creation with schedules and documentation to support the claim; meetings to assess claim methodology and requirements; preparation of responses to inquiries.
4. Resolution. Tasks include: Written, telephonic and person-to-person communications; identification of potential differences; assistance in resolution. In an effort to save costs and allow KPMG to complete the needed work within the budget: ¢ Metro will be responsible for resolving the Annual Aggregate Retention claims with Travelers. e Metro will perform the internal searching, locating, and production of documents needed to evaluate and support the fire claim. Metro will apprise KPMG of the location and people with full knowledge of such documents, so the accounting analysis can proceed efficiently. e Request for advances and submission of claim may be drafted by KPMG but submitted by Metro. L-¢¥0 CONTRACT WITH KPMG LLP FOR CONSULTATION AND/OR FORENSIC ACCOUNTANT SERVICES WHEREAS, the Department of Law of The Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County is required by Section 8.602 of the Charter of the Metropolitan Government to “supervise, direct and control all of the law work of the metropolitan government .. . , to furnish legal advice to... all... boards and commissions concerning any matters arising in connection with the exercise of their official powers or performance of their official duties . . . [and to rJepresent the metropolitan government in all litigation . . .;” and, WHEREAS, Section 4.04.020.C.5 of the Metropolitan Code of Laws exempts the Department of Law from the requirements of the Procurement Code “in the acquisition of... consultant . . . and other services required in litigation or other legal representation of the metropolitan government; and, WHEREAS, the Department of Law has determined that it is in need of a consultant and/or Forensic Accountant Services in the matter of the fire at the Nashville Thermal Transfer Plant on May 23, 2002; and, WHEREAS, the Department of Law has determined that KPMG LLP, has the necessary expertise to provide these services; NOW, THEREFORE, THE PARTIES AGREE AS FOLLOWS: This Contract is entered into on this 14th day of October, 2002, by and between the Department of Law of The Metropolitan Government of Nas atid’ Davidson County (“Metro”) and KPMG LLP (“Contractor”), This Contract: this document and the Comprehensive Travel Regulations of the Metropolitan Nashville and Davidson County, attached as Exhibit A and incorporated-herein by referencé.
1. Purpose. Contractor agrees to provide and Metro agrees to purchase the following services: Forensic Accountant Services to the Metropolitan Government related to determining the costs to the Metropolitan Government associated with the fire at the Nashville Thermal Transfer Plant earlier this year. The services will include investigation, consulting and, if needed, testimony.
2. Term. Services shall be provided on an as needed basis, upon the request of the Department of Law, fromi the effective date of this agreement until the completion of any litigation, arbitration and/or administrative proceeding resulting from the above-referenced fire 3 Compensation. Contractor shall be paid professional fees of $295 Dollars per hour, plus reasonable expenses, for accident reconstruction services, coordination of digital imaging services and trial preparation. The fee for testimony and services at trial shall be $370 Dollars per hour for a director, and $425 Dollars per hour for a partner. Said amounts are to be D:\Documents and Settings\annabrown\Desktop\ContractK PMG.doc ARCHIVE
billed on a monthly basis for the services rendered during the preceding month. Reimbursement for travel expenses shall not exceed the rates specified in the Comprehensive Travel Regulations of Metro, which is attached hereto as Exhibit A. There will be no other charges or fees for the performance of this Contract. The total compensation paid to Contractor (including expenses) under this Contract shall not exceed $20,000 Dollars without prior authorization. All payments by Metro shall be made within approximately thirty (30) days of receipt of invoice. Invoices are not required for any month(s) during which services are not provided. If any party desires to take the deposition of Contractor, Contractor must arrange with that party independently for reimbursement of Contractor for all fees and expenses associated with any deposition.
4. Termination--Breach. Should Contractor fail to fulfill in a timely and proper manner his obligations under this Contract, or if he should violate any of the terms of this Contract, Metro shall have the right to immediately terminate the Contract and withhold payments that are in excess of fair compensation for work completed. Such termination shall not relieve Contractor of any liability to Metro for damages sustained by virtue of any breach by Contractor.
5. Termination--Funding. Should funding for this Contract be discontinued, Metro shall have the rights to terminate the Contract upon written notice to Contractor.
6. Termination--Notice. Metro may terminate this Contract at any time upon thirty (30) days written notice to Contractor.
7. Compliance with Laws. Contractor agrees to comply with any applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations.
8. Notices. Notices to Metro shall be sent to: Karl F. Dean, Director Department of Law 204 Metropolitan Courthouse Nashville, TN 37201 Notices to Contractor shall be sent to: Phillip D. Ostwalt 303 Peachtree St. NE Atlanta, GA 30308
9. Limitation of Liability. maximum liability to the Metropolitan Government arising for any reason relating to Contractor’s performance of this Contract or any amendment thereto shall be limited to the amount of fees paid to Contractor for its performance. Neither party shall have any liability to the other party for any lost profits or special, incidental, ARCHIVE
indirect or consequential damages, even if such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages.
10. Maintenance of Records. Contractor shall maintain documentation for all charges against Metro. The books, records, and documents of Contractor, insofar as they relate to work performed or money received under the Contract, shall be maintained for a period of three (3) full years from the date of final payment and will be subject to audit, at any reasonable time and upon reasonable notice by Metro or its duly appointed representatives. The records shall be maintained in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. 11, Metro Property. Any Metro property, including but not limited to, books, records, and equipment, that is in Contractor’s possession shall be maintained by Contractor in good condition and repair, and shall be returned to Metro by Contractor upon termination of the Contract. All goods, documents, records, and other work product and property produced during the performance of this Contract are deemed to be Metro property.
12. Modification of Contract. This Contract may be modified only by written amendment executed by all parties and their signatories hereto. 13, Partnership/Joint Venture. Nothing herein shall in any way be construed or intended to create a partnership or joint venture between the parties or to create the relationship of principal and agent between or among any of the parties. None of the parties hereto shall hold itself out in a manner contrary to the terms of this paragraph. No party shall become liable for any representation, act, or omission of any other party contrary to the terms of this paragraph. 14, Waiver. No waiver of any provision of this Contract shall affect the right of any party thereafter to enforce such provision or to exercise any right or remedy available to it in the event of any other default.
15. Employment. Contractor shall not subscribe to any personnel policy which permits or allows for the promotion, demotion, employment, dismissal or laying off of any individual due to his race, creed, color, national origin, age, sex, or which is in violation of applicable laws concerning the employment of individuals with disabilities.
16. Contingent Fees. Contractor hereby represents that Contractor has not been retained or retained any persons to solicit or secure a Metropolitan Government contract upon an agreement or understanding for a contingent commission, percentage, or brokerage fee, except for retention of bona fide employees or bona fide established commercial selling agencies for the purpose of securing business. Breach of the provisions of this paragraph is, in addition to a breach of this Contract, a breach of ethical standards which may result in civil or criminal sanction and/or debarment or suspension from being a contractor or subcontractor under Metropolitan Government contracts.
17. Gratuities and Kickbacks. It shall be a breach of ethical standards for any person to offer, give or agree to give, any employee or former employee, or for any employee or former employee to solicit, demand, accept, or agree to accept from another person, a gratuity or an ARCHIVE
offer of employment in connection with any decision, approval, disapproval, recommendation, preparation of any part of a program requirement or a purchase request, influencing the content of any specification or procurement standard, rendering of advice, investigation, auditing or in any other advisory capacity in any proceeding or application, request for ruling, determination, claim or controversy or other particular matter, pertaining to any program requirement of a contract or subcontract or to any solicitation or proposal therefor. It shall be a breach of ethical standards for any payment, gratuity or offer of employment to be made by or on behalf of a subcontractor under a contract to the prime contractor or higher tier subcontractor or any person associated therewith, as an inducement for the award of a subcontract or order. Breach of the provisions of this paragraph is, in addition to a breach of this Contract, a breach of ethical standards which may result in civil or criminal sanction and/or debarment or suspension from being a contractor or subcontractor under the Metropolitan Government contracts.
18. Assignment - Consent Required. The provisions of this Contract shall inure to the benefit of and shall be binding upon the respective successors and assignees of the parties hereto. Neither this Contract nor any of the rights and obligations of Contractor hereunder shall be assigned or transferred in whole or in part without the prior written consent of Metro. Any such assignment or transfer shall not release Contractor from its obligations hereunder. NOTICE OF ASSIGNMENT OF ANY RIGHTS TO MONEY DUE THE CONTRACTOR UNDER THIS CONTRACT MUST BE SENT TO THE ATTENTION OF METRO'S CHIEF ACCOUNTANT, DIVISION OF ACCOUNTS, DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE, 222 THIRD AVENUE NORTH, SUITE 750, NASHVILLE, TN 37201.
19. Entire Contract. This Contract sets forth the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and shall govern the respective duties and obligations of the parties.
20. Force Majeure. No party shall have any liability to the other hereunder by reasons of any delay or failure to perform any obligation or covenant if the delay or failure to perform is occasioned by the force majeure, meaning any act of God, storm, fire casualty, work stoppage, strike, lockout, labor dispute, civil disturbance, riot, war, national emergency, act of Government, act of public enemy, or other cause of similar or dissimilar nature beyond its control.
21. Governing Law. The validity, construction, and effect of this Contract and any and all extensions and/or modifications thereof shall be governed by the laws of the State of Tennessee.
22. Severability. Should any provision of this Contract be declared to be invalid by any court of competent jurisdiction, such provision shall be severed and shall not affect the validity of the remaining provisions of this Contract.
23. Effective Date. This Contract shall not be binding upon the parties until it has been signed first by the Contractor and then by the authorized representatives of the Metropolitan ARCHIVE
Government and has been filed in the office of the Metropolitan Clerk. When it has been so signed and filed, this Contract shall be effective as of the date first written above.
